learn.title: More than two paths
learn.body: Sometimes there are more than two outcomes, like grades. Chain tests with `else if`. C checks them from the top and runs the first block whose condition is true, then skips the rest.

learn.title: A grade chain
learn.body: 75 fails the first test but passes the second.

learn.title: Order matters
learn.body: Because the first true test wins, put the narrowest or highest tests first. If we tested `score >= 70` before `score >= 90`, a 95 would stop at B. The final `else` catches everything left over.

learn.title: switch
learn.body: When you compare one whole number or char against fixed values, `switch` can be neater. Each `case` is a possible value. `break` jumps out of the switch. `default` is the catch-all, like a final `else`.

learn.title: A switch
learn.body: `day` is 2, so the program jumps to `case 2`.

learn.title: Forgetting break
learn.body: Without `break`, execution falls through into the next case. Starting at `case 1`, a missing break prints `one` and then also `two`. Sometimes that is wanted, but usually it is a bug, so add `break` on purpose.
A `switch` works on ints and chars only, not on decimals or text.

questions.prompt: `score = 75`, with chain tests for 90, then 70, then `else`. What prints?
questions.explanation: 75 is not at least 90, but it is at least 70, so B runs.

questions.prompt: In an `if`, `else if`, `else` chain, how many blocks run?
questions.explanation: The first true condition wins and the rest are skipped.

questions.prompt: In a switch, \_\_ jumps out of the switch.
questions.explanation: Without `break`, execution continues into the next case.

questions.prompt: The catch-all label in a switch is \_\_.
`n = 1`, with `case 1` and `case 2` printing one and two, and no breaks. What prints?
questions.explanation: Execution starts at `case 1` and falls through to `case 2`.

questions.prompt: Which can be the value of a `switch`?
questions.explanation: In C a switch works on integer types, and a char counts as one.

questions.explanation: From strictest to loosest, then the catch-all.
